author: reek
body: `Real trapping` traps when a result leaves the finite range, on a NaN or on either infinity. This half of the coverage is the negative control: every value here is finite, several of them by a very small margin, and none may trap. A guard that fired on anything near the boundary would kill this test rather than fail it, which is a loud failure and the point of choosing these operands.

author: reek
body: The positive half cannot live here. A trap is a `UD2` and takes the machine with it, so it has no output to compare; `real-trapping-overflow` carries it behind a `.fatal` sidecar, the same split `bounded-param-trap` already uses.

author: reek
body: This test used to add 3.0 and 4.0 and nothing else. That exercised addition, not the mode: it never produced a NaN or an infinity, which is the only thing trapping is for, and the emitter checked for NaN alone and ignored infinity entirely for as long as the mode existed.

author: reek
body: Bit patterns, not decimals: the largest finite double and infinity render alike, and the near-boundary operands below have no short decimal form.
